quizzes.prompt: Your account’s on GitHub.com. Which button signs you in to the app?

targets.label: Sign in to GitHub Enterprise Cloud (*.ghe.com)
targets.feedback: That one’s for organizations on `*.ghe.com`. An account on GitHub.com uses **Sign in to GitHub**.

explain.correct: Right: **Sign in to GitHub**. Then sign in with your GitHub account.
explain.wrong: Pick the button for an account on GitHub.com.

hints: Two buttons, two kinds of account.
The second one is only for `*.ghe.com`.
Select **Sign in to GitHub**, the green one.

quizzes.prompt: Where do you start adding your fork to the app?

targets.label: + in the prompt box
targets.feedback: That **+** belongs to the prompt box. The heading above your projects has its own **+** in the sidebar.

targets.label: New
targets.feedback: **New** starts new work. Adding a project starts from the heading above your projects.

targets.label: Customize
targets.feedback: **Customize** is where you extend the app. Look beside the heading above your projects.

explain.correct: Right! The **+** next to **Sessions** opens the menu for adding a project. This picture’s from an older app version, where that heading read **Projects**.
explain.wrong: Close! Look for the **+** beside the heading above your projects: **Sessions** in the app, **Projects** in this older picture.

hints: Your projects live in the sidebar.
Find the heading above your projects. It’s **Sessions** in the app (this picture still says **Projects**). There’s a small button beside it.
Select the **+** to the right of that heading.

quizzes.situation: You select **Add GitHub repository** and search for `copilot-app-for-beginners`. Say two results come up: `github/copilot-app-for-beginners` and `{fork}`.

options.feedback: That’s the original. Your practice work belongs in your fork, and the setup script refuses to change the original.

options.text: Either one. They have the same files
options.feedback: They start out the same, but only your fork is yours to change. The setup script refuses the original.

explain.correct: Right. Pick your fork, the result that starts with your GitHub username. The app clones it and adds it to the sidebar.
explain.wrong: Your practice work belongs in your own copy of the course.

quizzes.prompt: For this one-time setup, where should the session run?

targets.label: New worktree
targets.feedback: The checkmark shows the default, **New worktree**, a separate directory for each session. For setup, change it to **Current checkout**.

targets.label: Cloud
targets.feedback: **Cloud** runs in a cloud sandbox. Setup uses the clone that’s already on your machine.

explain.correct: Yes: **Current checkout** works in the existing checkout, the clone already on your machine. You’ll meet the other options on Thousand-Bough Isle.
explain.wrong: Setup should use the copy that’s already on your machine.

hints: Don’t trust the checkmark. It just shows the default.
You want the option that works in the clone already on your machine.

quizzes.situation: You run `gh auth status` in **Terminal** and it says you’re logged in as **someone-else**, not the account that owns your fork.

options.text: Run `gh auth login`, choose **GitHub.com** → **Login with a web browser**, then run `gh auth status` again
Ignore it. The app’s sign-in covers the CLI too
options.feedback: GitHub CLI has its own sign-in, separate from the app.
The CLI works fine. It’s just signed in to the wrong account.

options.text: Run the setup script with `--yes` anyway
options.feedback: The script acts as GitHub CLI’s account, and it stops if that account doesn’t own your fork. Sign in as the right account first.

explain.correct: Right. Sign in with `gh auth login`, then confirm the active account with `gh auth status`.
explain.wrong: The CLI’s account has to match your fork before you continue.

quizzes.situation: In **Terminal**, `node -v` prints `v20.19.5`. The Node.js download page marks v24 as **LTS**.

options.text: Carry on. It printed a version number, so Node.js is installed
options.feedback: A number means it’s installed, but for Node.js the course also compares the first number with the LTS. 20 is lower than 24.

options.text: Install the LTS version, then run `node -v` again
Reinstall Git, Node.js, npm, and GitHub CLI
options.feedback: Install only what’s missing or out of date. Here that’s just Node.js.

options.text: Run `node -v` again until it prints a newer version
options.feedback: It prints the same version until you install a newer Node.js. Install the LTS first, then check again.

explain.correct: Right. Your first number is lower than the LTS, so install the LTS version, then run the checks again.
explain.wrong: Compare Node’s first number with the LTS on the download page.

quizzes.situation: You want to send: “Give me an overview of the copilot-app-for-beginners course repository. Focus on the learning path and the samples/book-app-web folder.”

options.text: The Copilot app’s prompt box (the speaking tube to the crew)

options.feedback: **Terminal** runs commands like `git --version`. Requests to the agent go in the prompt box.

explain.correct: Yes! Requests go to the agent through the prompt box. It should summarize the course and point out `samples/book-app-web`.
explain.wrong: Terminal is for commands. Who should answer this request?

quizzes.prompt: Put the five setup steps in order. Each one depends on the step before it.

items.text: Add your fork: **+** by **Sessions** → **Add GitHub repository**
Start a project session on **Current checkout**

explain.correct: That’s the whole voyage: fork, add it, a **Current checkout** session, preview, then run it for real.
explain.wrong: You can’t add a fork you haven’t made, and the preview always comes before `--yes`.

quizzes.prompt: Setup hops between GitHub.com and the app. Match each step to where you do it.

left.text: Turn on workflows for your fork

explain.correct: That’s it. Workflows live in your fork’s **Actions** tab on GitHub.com, the workspace selector sits below the prompt box, commands go in **Terminal**, and requests go in the prompt box.
explain.wrong: Workflows are a GitHub.com setting. In the app, commands and requests go to different places.

quizzes.prompt: What does the setup script create in your fork? Pick all that apply.

explain.correct: Yes: labels, issues, practice branches, and pull requests. The bugs stay on practice branches, never `main`.
explain.wrong: Four of these are right. The intentional bugs stay off `main`.

quizzes.prompt: Why enable workflows on your fork?

options.text: So GitHub can run the automated checks for the practice exercises
So you can sign in to the app
So the app can clone the repository

explain.correct: Right. New forks switch GitHub Actions off, and the practice checks need them.
explain.wrong: These are GitHub Actions workflows. The app’s Automations are something else.

quizzes.prompt: The setup script creates items on GitHub in your fork. What do you run first?

options.text: `--dry-run`, to preview its target and planned changes

options.feedback: `--yes` runs the setup for real. Preview it with `--dry-run` first.
That’s only for an organization fork you’re authorized to set up, after you’ve checked the `Repository:` line.

explain.correct: Right. The script creates items on GitHub in your fork, so you’ll preview its target and planned changes before running it.
explain.wrong: Preview first: the script creates items on GitHub in your fork.

quizzes.situation: The preview reports `Repository: github/copilot-app-for-beginners` and ends with `Dry run complete. No changes were made.` You meant to set up your fork.
quizzes.prompt: What should you do before running `--yes`?

options.text: Stop and rerun `--dry-run` from your fork. Continue only when `Repository:` names it.
Run `--yes`; the dry run finished without errors.
options.feedback: The output names the original course repository, not your fork. Check the `Repository:` line before continuing.

options.text: Run the same dry run again, then use `--yes` if it finishes the same way.
options.feedback: A successful preview does not change its target. The `Repository:` line must name your fork before you continue.

explain.correct: Right. Confirm `Repository:` shows your fork before you run the setup for real.
explain.wrong: This preview names the original repository. Check the target before running `--yes`.

quizzes.situation: Your version checks print `command not found` for `git --version`, `v24.22.1` for `node -v` (the download page marks v24 as **LTS**), `11.19.1` for `npm -v`, and `gh version 2.74.0`.
quizzes.prompt: What do you do before the setup script?

options.feedback: Its first number, 24, matches the LTS, so Node.js is fine. It’s Git that’s missing.

options.text: Install Git, then run the checks again

options.feedback: Install only the tools that are missing. Node.js, npm and GitHub CLI each printed a version.

options.text: Carry on to the setup script
options.feedback: Git printed no version, so it’s missing. Install it first, then run the checks again.

explain.correct: Right. Install only what’s missing, then run the checks again before you continue.
explain.wrong: Every check should print a version. Which one didn’t?

quizzes.situation: The dry-run finishes and shows `Repository: someone-else/copilot-app-for-beginners`.

options.text: Stop, and point it at your fork before running `--yes`
Run `--yes`. The preview is only a suggestion

explain.correct: Yes. The `Repository:` line has to show your fork before you run it for real.
explain.wrong: The preview exists so you catch exactly this. Don’t run it against someone else’s repository.

quizzes.prompt: Which of these do you need before you start? Pick all that apply.

options.text: A Copilot plan, or your own model provider

explain.correct: That’s the list. Your editor is welcome, but it isn’t required for setup.
explain.wrong: Five of these are prerequisites. One is nice to have but not required.

quizzes.prompt: Your fork shows under **Sessions**. How do you start the session you’ll run setup in?

options.feedback: That **+** adds another project. Each project has its own **+** for a new session.
A chat isn’t tied to your repository. Setup runs in a project session.

explain.correct: Right. The **+** beside the project starts a project session in it.
explain.wrong: Look beside the project itself, not the **Sessions** heading.

quizzes.prompt: Later chapters work in the course’s web sample app. Which folder is it in?

options.feedback: That’s where the setup script lives.
The root holds the chapters. The sample app has its own folder under `samples`.
Those are the course’s reference pages, like the Training GitHub Scenarios appendix.

explain.correct: Yes: `samples/book-app-web` is the course’s main sample app, the one the overview flagged.
explain.wrong: The overview prompt asked about it by name.

quizzes.situation: The script finished, but the practice issues weren’t created in your fork.

options.text: Enable **Issues** in the fork’s **Settings → Features**, then rerun the script
Delete the fork and start over

explain.correct: Yes. Forks can have Issues turned off. Turn them on and rerun.
explain.wrong: Nothing’s broken. A repository feature is just switched off.

pages.title: Get the Copilot app
pages.caption: Download and install the **GitHub Copilot app** for your system from [github.com/features/ai/github-app](https://github.com/features/ai/github-app). Open it and select **Sign in to GitHub** (on `*.ghe.com`, **Sign in to GitHub Enterprise Cloud**). At **Connect your repositories**, leave every repository unselected and select **Continue**.

pages.title: What you need
pages.caption: A GitHub account, and a Copilot plan **or** your own model provider. On Copilot Business or Enterprise, your organization has to enable the **GitHub Copilot app** policy. Install [Git](https://git-scm.com/install), [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/download) (the version marked **LTS**, for the course’s sample app), and [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com) (`gh`, for the one-time setup script). You’ll check their versions in the app’s **Terminal** once your fork is connected.

pages.title: The New view
pages.caption: Select **Continue**, and the app opens the **New** view, where new work starts. If it shows a short tip about a new feature, you can close the tip.

pages.title: Fork the course
pages.caption: Fork the course repository on GitHub at [github.com/github/copilot-app-for-beginners/fork](https://github.com/github/copilot-app-for-beginners/fork). Your practice work, and the practice items the setup script adds, go in your fork, not the original.

pages.title: Add your fork
pages.caption: **+** next to **Sessions** → **Add GitHub repository**, search for `copilot-app-for-beginners`, and pick your fork, not the original. Already have a local copy? **Open folder**. Have your fork’s URL? **Clone repository**, paste it in **Repository URL**, then select **Clone**. If the app says Git is missing, install Git and try again. This picture’s from an older app version, where **Sessions** was called **Projects**.

pages.title: A Current checkout session
pages.caption: Point to your project in the sidebar and select the **+** that appears to start a project session. Sessions start on **New worktree** by default. For setup, pick **Current checkout** in the workspace selector below the prompt box, so it runs in the clone already on your machine. Then submit this short prompt to create the session.
pages.code: Name the top-level folders in this repository. Do not change any files.

pages.title: Terminal in the app
pages.caption: Select **View → Toggle Review Panel**, then **Terminal**. No tab? Select **+**, then **Terminal**. Commands run here: the version checks, `gh auth status`, and the setup script. Each check should print a version. For `node -v`, compare the first number with the **LTS** on the [Node.js download page](https://nodejs.org/en/download): lower means install the LTS. Install only what’s missing, then run the checks again. On Windows, if PowerShell won’t load `npm.ps1`, use `npm.cmd` in place of `npm`, or, if your organization allows it, run `Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser`. Requests to the agent go in the prompt box.
pages.code:
git --version
node -v
npm -v
gh --version
gh auth status   # signed in as the account that owns your fork?
gh auth login    # if not: GitHub.com → Login with a web browser

pages.title: Turn on workflows
pages.caption: New forks start with GitHub Actions switched off. On GitHub.com, open your fork’s **Actions** tab and select **I understand my workflows, go ahead and enable them** so the practice checks can run.

pages.title: The practice checks
pages.caption: With workflows on, GitHub runs automated checks on your fork’s pull requests. One of the practice pull requests has a check that fails on purpose, so you can fix it in a later chapter.

pages.title: The setup commands
pages.caption: Run both in **Terminal**, from the repository root (the folder with `.github` and `samples`). Preview first, check the `Repository:` line, then run it for real.
pages.code:
node .github/scripts/setup-training-scenarios.js --dry-run   # preview; check Repository:
node .github/scripts/setup-training-scenarios.js --yes       # wait for "Setup complete."

pages.title: Learn about the course
pages.caption: Back in your project session, send this from the **prompt box**, not **Terminal**. The reply should sum up the course structure and point out `samples/book-app-web`, the web sample for later exercises. Models vary, so yours will be worded differently.
pages.code: Give me an overview of the copilot-app-for-beginners course repository. Focus on the learning path and the samples/book-app-web folder.

pages.title: Soundcheck
pages.caption: Setting up the app is like prepping a studio before the first take.

pages.title: I can’t sign in
pages.caption: Check you’re on the expected GitHub account, with a Copilot plan or your own model provider. Your organization has to leave the **GitHub Copilot app** policy on, and that’s separate from the Copilot CLI policy. On `*.ghe.com`? Select **Sign in to GitHub Enterprise Cloud**.

pages.title: I can’t see the repository
pages.caption: Check you’ve got access to it on GitHub and that you picked the right account or organization. Already cloned it? Try **Open folder**. If the app says Git is missing, install Git and retry. A chat can’t explain the repository? Check the right one’s connected, your prompt names `copilot-app-for-beginners`, and the app has permission to read the project folder.

pages.title: The script stops for an organization fork
pages.caption: The setup script won’t change a repository an organization owns. Add `--allow-shared-repository` only if you’re authorized to set up that organization fork and the `Repository:` line shows the right target.

pages.title: The script stops with “Setup failed”
pages.caption: Read the message after `Setup failed`. Fix the problem it reports, then run the script with `--yes` again. It reuses the labels, issues, branches, and pull requests it already made, so you won’t get duplicates.

pages.title: Practice items weren’t created
pages.caption: Issues missing from your fork? On GitHub.com, open your fork’s **Settings** → **Features**, turn on **Issues**, and rerun the script. Can’t run the script at all? The course’s Training GitHub Scenarios appendix has the manual steps. Do them before Chapter 02.

glossary.definition: Your own copy of a repository on GitHub.
A session that works inside one of your projects (repositories).
Run a session in the existing checkout: the clone that’s already on your machine.
A separate working copy of your repository, so a session’s changes stay out of your way.
The app’s side panel, with tabs such as Changes and Terminal. Open it with View → Toggle Review Panel.
Automated checks and jobs that GitHub runs for a repository. Not the same as the app’s Automations, which are saved agent tasks.
A preview that shows what a command would do without changing anything.

gear.rack.checks.text: git --version, node -v, npm -v and gh --version each print a version number.

gear.rack.lantern.text: node -v prints v20.19.5 first, lower than the LTS (v24), so you install the LTS and run it again: v24.22.1.

gear.rack.rope.windows.text: On Windows, PowerShell may refuse to load npm.ps1. Use npm.cmd in place of npm (npm.cmd -v), or, if your organization allows it, run Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser.

gear.rack.signedIn.text: $ gh auth status → ✓ Logged in to github.com account your-handle

P0.2.dryRun.text: --dry-run → Repository: {repository} … Dry run complete. No changes were made.

P0.2.notARepo.text: Run this script from the root of a cloned Git repository.

P0.2.cargo.text: Labels, issues, practice branches and pull requests (9, 5, 7 and 3).
